---
title: "Roadmap and open questions"
description: "What is still undecided or unproven — and where feedback helps most."
---

These workflows are in active use but still settling. This page lists what
is already known to be open, so you don't have to ask — and where your
experience would help decide.

## How to give feedback {#feedback}

For now, open an [issue](https://github.com/nfdi4health/datashield-workflows/issues):
a missing input, a behaviour that doesn't fit your package, an idea, or a
point from the list below.

::: {.callout-note}
## Please no pull requests for now
The repository has no branch model or review rules yet, so pull requests
can't be handled properly. Please open an issue instead — pull requests
may be closed without review until this is set up.
:::

## Recent changes {#recent-changes}

**Version 1**

The first versioned release. Callers have to change a few lines once;
after that, breaking changes only come with a new major version.

**What callers need to change:**

- **New address:** the repository moved to
  `nfdi4health/datashield-workflows`. Change the `uses:` lines of your
  callers; the old path `FlorianSchw/package-workflows` still redirects
  for now, but may stop doing so.
- **Federation rules** in the Claude Console: change each rule to the
  [CEL expression](claude-setup.qmd#setting-up-a-repository). It admits
  the new path at any version (`@main`, `@v1`, a test branch); the rule
  IDs, and so your secrets, stay the same.
- **Renamed inputs** of the roxygen and test suggestions — a caller still
  using an old name fails at the start:
  - `scan-mode` → `review-scope`, with the values `changed` (default)
    and `all`;
  - `sweep-base` → `review-branch`;
  - `datashield: true` is gone: `datashield-type` alone says it
    (`none` by default, else `client`, `server` or `utility`).
- **Package release:** the inputs `config-repo` and `config-ref` are
  gone; the shared release configuration comes from the version of the
  workflows you call.
- **Permissions:** the roxygen and test caller jobs grant
  `actions: read` and `checks: read`, or GitHub refuses to start the
  run.
- **Settings files** of your own (e.g. `config/bot-authors.json`) are
  now YAML and merged over the shared ones key by key, see
  [adjusting the guidance](suggestions.qmd#adjusting-the-guidance). An
  old JSON copy is no longer read; `accept_reasons` moved from
  `config/claude.yml` to `config/suggestion-policy.yml`.

**New and changed:**

- **Scheduled and manual runs review only what changed** since the
  branch's last review, read from the workflow's earlier runs — no more
  monthly sweeps with a rotating share. A **full review** of every file is
  `review-scope: all`, offered in the example callers as a choice in
  "Run workflow". Its pull request is
  `bot-suggest/<kind>-all-<branch>-YYYY-MM`, titled "…: full review". See
  [scheduled and manual runs](suggestions.qmd#scheduled-runs).
- **[Choosing suggestions](suggestion-choices.qmd) by checkbox:** untick
  a suggestion you don't want, or tick one that wasn't applied, and the
  bot's branch follows. Needs one more caller.
- **One report per suggestion PR**, rebuilt on every run: findings with
  the commit they came from, outdated ones crossed out, a "Latest review"
  line. With a suggestion PR open, the bots build on what it proposes.
- **The bots' rules in one file,** `config/suggestion-policy.yml`:
  reasons, limits, possible bugs, author roles, and
  [where reports go](suggestions.qmd#where-reports-go).
- **Possible bugs in the code** come with Claude's verdict and how sure
  it is; set which are reported with `code-issue-confidence`. The test
  suggestions open one issue per function, at high confidence only, and
  don't file the same failing test again.
- **Test suggestions** declare packages the new tests use in
  `Suggests`, and run the generated tests without any tokens.
- **Analysis scripts** are written step by step, each tested with the
  ones before it; a step can name the steps it builds on with
  [`depends_on`](datashield-analysis-details.qmd#the-plans-fields).
- **Failed Claude calls** are retried; a call that still fails leaves a
  warning, the run stays green, and the file is checked again next run.
- **Releases** read commits with the `conventionalcommits` preset, so
  `feat!:` makes a major release too, see
  [package release](package-release.qmd#configuration).

**October 2026**

- **Usage counting:** every run of the bot suggestions (roxygen, tests,
  authors) and the DataSHIELD analysis scripts is now counted once,
  anonymously, so their usage can be reported per workflow, outcome and
  version. Nothing about
  your repository is sent; see [Usage counting](getting-started.qmd#usage-counting).
- **Test suggestions find all test files of a function**, also
  `test-<category>-<function>.R` as in the DataSHIELD base packages. In a
  repository named that way, new tests go into the file of the category
  Claude picks. See [test files](test-suggest.qmd#test-files).
- **Tests connect the way yours already do.** A DSLite test setup is now
  only created if your tests have no way to connect yet; set with the new
  input [`dslite-setup`](test-suggest-datashield.qmd#connecting). If your
  tests connect via Opal or Armadillo and you want the DSLite setup
  anyway, set `dslite-setup: create`.
- **Bot suggestions on push, and only what's new.** The roxygen, test and
  author suggestions can also run on pushes to your working branches.
  After a pull request's first run, they review only what is new since the
  last run, and an open suggestion PR collects the new suggestions instead
  of being rebuilt. See [how suggestions work](suggestions.qmd#what-gets-reviewed).
  - **Manual runs:** "Run workflow" now sweeps the branch you choose,
    not always `dev`.
  - **Sweep branch names** include the branch:
    `bot-suggest/<kind>-sweep-<branch>-YYYY-MM`. An open sweep PR of the
    current month under the old name is left behind once and can be
    closed.
  - **No change needed** in existing callers; the `scan-mode` line in
    the examples is no longer needed.
- **Roxygen callers need `issues: write`.** Possible code bugs found in a
  sweep without a suggestion PR now go to a monthly issue instead of
  only the job log. **Add `issues: write`** to the roxygen caller's
  `permissions`, or GitHub refuses to start the run.
- **New: [DataSHIELD analysis scripts](datashield-analysis-suggest.qmd)**
  for analysis projects set up with dsAnalysis.
- **New `datashield-type: utility`** for analyst-side helper packages,
  in the [roxygen](roxygen-suggest.qmd#datashield-packages) and
  [test](test-suggest-datashield.qmd#utility) suggestions. An unknown
  `datashield-type` now stops the run.

## Open questions

### The analysis plan

The [analysis plan](datashield-analysis-details.qmd#the-plans-fields) is a
first draft, and its shape will change with experience.

*Feedback wanted:* fields a real analysis plan needs, and what is easy or
hard to fill in.

### Versioning

Version 1 is the first versioned release: `@v1` follows its compatible
updates, breaking changes come as `@v2`. `@main` keeps getting every
change first. The examples still reference `@main` until `v1` is
published.

*Feedback wanted:* inputs you miss, or ones you never need.

### Suggestion thresholds

Bot suggestions are only proposed for [certain reasons](suggestions.qmd#what-gets-proposed):
documentation that is missing, inaccurate or incomplete, and tests that
cover a new code path, an error, an edge case or a likely regression.
These lists are a first setting.

*Feedback wanted:* suggestion PRs that weren't worth it, or improvements
you expected but didn't get.

### ~~Model per task~~

~~All suggestion workflows currently use the same Claude model. Tests
arguably deserve a stronger one, since deciding which tests add value — or
could be deleted — needs more careful reasoning than documentation.~~
Done: the [test suggestions](test-suggest.qmd) use a stronger model with
extended thinking.

### Release options

Releases are currently created as drafts, to be published by hand, and
don't comment on the issues and pull requests they include. A comment such
as "Included in version 1.2.0" on fixed issues would be a useful record,
but needs an additional GitHub App permission.

*Feedback wanted:* drafts or direct publishing? Comments on released
issues?

## Not yet proven in real use

- **Scheduled runs** reviewing what changed since the last review: the
  first is still ahead. Full reviews and the checkboxes work.
- **Changes to existing tests**: updating and deleting them, and reporting
  possible bugs. Generating, running and proposing new tests works.
- **The first real release** with the version written to `DESCRIPTION` —
  the release chain has so far only run as a dry run.
- ~~**[Workflow graphs](workflow-graphs.qmd)**: new; the first real runs
  are still ahead.~~ Running on a first repository; the layout is still
  being refined.
- **Suggestions on push**: tested locally; the first real runs are
  still ahead. Building on an open suggestion PR works.
- **[DataSHIELD analysis scripts](datashield-analysis-suggest.qmd)**:
  tested locally with real DSLite runs; the first real runs, with Claude,
  the package installs and the step-by-step drafting, are still ahead.
- **`datashield-type: utility`**: the first real runs are still ahead.
